title: Client Account Administrator

description:

title: HR Administrator
company: ACS Recruitment Solutions Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
HR Administrator
Kettering, Hybrid working
£28,500 per annum
Monday - Friday, Full time permanent

We're working with a growingUK-wide HR consultancy that provides practical, people-focused HR support to businesses across a wide range of sectors.

Due to continued growth, they are looking for an organised, proactive and service-focused HR Administrator to join their central team. This is a varied position offering the chance to work closely with experienced HR professionals while supporting a diverse client base.

The role would suit either a HR administrator who enjoys variety, takes pride in producing accurate work and wants to develop their career within a consultancy environment, or someone that is at the start of their HR career ready to develop their hands on experience.

Key Responsibilities:

You'll provide essential administrative support across a broad range of HR activities, helping ensure clients receive an efficient, professional and reliable service.

Working alongside HR Consultants and Advisors, you'll have exposure to different businesses and a wide variety of HR processes, giving you the opportunity to develop your knowledge and experience across the employee lifecycle.
- Providing accurate and efficient HR administration across a portfolio of clients.
- Preparing and maintaining employment documentation, including contracts, policies, handbooks and employee letters.
- Reviewing and updating client documentation to reflect legislative changes and business requirements.
- Producing documentation relating to contractual changes, employee relations matters and other HR processes.
- Coordinating new starter administration, including contracts, references, pre-employment checks and onboarding paperwork.
- Supporting recruitment campaigns, including preparing adverts, reviewing applications, arranging interviews and communicating with candidates and clients.
- Providing administrative assistance to HR Consultants and Advisors with employee relations and other HR casework.
- Preparing meeting notes, supporting documentation and evidence packs.
- Acting as a reliable point of contact for clients regarding day-to-day HR administration.
- Monitoring shared inboxes and ensuring queries are dealt with promptly or escalated appropriately.
- Maintaining accurate client records, CRM information and internal systems.
- Managing and supporting client HR systems, developing strong system knowledge and becoming a key point of contact for users.
- Assisting with HR system demonstrations and supporting clients with system-related queries.
- Producing client reports covering workforce information such as absence, annual leave and turnover.
- Supporting internal projects, process improvements and wider administrative activities.
- Keeping up to date with developments in UK employment legislation and HR best practice.
- Maintaining strict confidentiality and ensuring appropriate data protection standards are followed.
- Providing additional administrative support to the wider consultancy team when required.

About You:
- Previous experience in an HR Administrator or similar HR support position is desirable.
- An understanding of HR administration and employee lifecycle processes.
- Experience handling confidential employee information.
- Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate work.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence communicating with clients and internal stakeholders.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft 365.
- Experience using HR and/or CRM systems.
- Experience with Breathe HR would be beneficial.
- An understanding of UK employment legislation and HR best practice.
- The ability to recognise when an issue requires escalation.
- A proactive approach and genuine interest in developing your HR career.
- CIPD Level 3 or above, currently working towards a CIPD qualification, or equivalent HR experience.

title: Contract Administrator
description:
Contract Administrator
Location: Chapel Brampton, Northampton
Hourly Rate: £13.45
Contract Type: Permanent
Working Hours: Monday-Friday 08:30 to 14:30 but can be flexible

About the role
Join us as a Contract Administrator and you will get to play an integral part in the provision of high-quality grounds services across your community. With strong communication and great organisational qualities, you will provide invaluable operations support to our landscaping contracts, working across different client and internal portals.

Responsibilities
Provide comprehensive office administration support, ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the office and maintaining a professional reception for visitors and callers.
Coordinate meetings, training sessions and events, including diary management, catering arrangements, minute-taking and maintaining key schedules.
Prepare, format and distribute correspondence, reports, emails and other business documentation as required.
Maintain accurate filing, record-keeping and archiving systems, ensuring company information is organised and accessible.
Support recruitment activities by advertising vacancies, liaising with job centres and managing candidate administration throughout the hiring process.
Administer employee lifecycle processes, including contracts, onboarding, leavers, HR records, training coordination and personnel file management.
Maintain workforce records, including holiday, sickness, PPE/uniform issuance and timesheet administration, while liaising with HR and Payroll on employee changes.
Manage purchase order processing, invoice administration and accounts queries using the company financial systems.
Produce and maintain financial reports, monitor contract costs, support month-end processes and ensure accurate recording of sales, variations and client payments.
Provide administrative support for regional tenders, contract operations and wider business activities, assisting managers and regional teams as required.

Requirements
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Prior experience in an administrative role managing helpdesks
Capable of dealing with a high workload and meeting deadlines
IT literate with a strong working knowledge of excel and an ability to pick up new systems
An eye for detail and problem-solving capabilities
Proficiency with basic Microsoft Office tools such as Excel.
Some CRM experience preferable - training will be provided on portals

Why join us?
As the UK's leading grounds maintenance and landscape creation provider, no two projects are ever the same - and neither are our people. That's why we're committed to nurturing a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.
We're proud to have been recognised as Employer of the Year and Sustainable Company of the Year at this year's Landscaper Awards, reflecting our commitment to supporting our people while delivering a more sustainable future.

What we offer
Career development: We offer career advancement and development opportunities through our bespoke apprenticeship programmes, our extensive in-house training academy, and coaching and mentorship.
Collaborative team environment: Join a diverse and inclusive workplace where you can collaborate with passionate and talented individuals.
Meaningful impact: Contribute to projects that make a real difference in the community and environment.

Benefits
Annual leave: 21 days holiday plus bank holidays
Family-friendly policies: Enhanced maternity and shared parental leave.
Employee Assistance Programmes: Support for personal and professional challenges.
Voluntary benefits: Discounts on retail, holidays, gym memberships, and more.
Financial wellbeing support: Resources to manage your finances.
Competitive pension scheme: Secure your future.
Recognition schemes: Colleague of the month and annual awards.
Volunteering policy: Two days per year to support a cause of your choice.
Mental health support: Comprehensive resources and support.

About our client
We are Europe's largest provider of grounds maintenance services and landscape creation, in the UK alone we're a community of over 3,000 passionate colleagues shaping the future of the green industry.

We understand what it means to grow. Our history dates back to 1919, and today, with a turnover of £250 million, we're more than just a company - we're a force for positive change. We offer a range of services to create, maintain, and manage landscapes across the UK.

Grow with us, and together we'll create a greener future for all.

If you receive suspicious outreach claiming to be from us, please contact us via the ManpowerGroup website.

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator
Salary: £27,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 5:00pm, with one hour for lunch
Contract: Full time, Permanent
Location: Northampton, Fully office based
Benefits: 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, birthday off, pension, free onsite parking

SMT Recruitment are delighted to be supporting a growing and established HR consultancy in the recruitment of an experienced HR Administrator to join their team.
This is an excellent opportunity for an HR professional who is looking to further develop their career within a varied and fast paced environment. Working within an outsourced HR setting, you will support a diverse portfolio of clients with their day to day HR requirements, gaining exposure to a broad range of businesses, employee matters and employment law.
The successful candidate will already have experience within an HR Administrator or HR support position and will be confident producing professional HR documentation, managing high volumes of administration and communicating with clients.

Key Responsibilities
As HR Administrator, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing day to day HR administration and support across a varied portfolio of clients
- Supporting with HR processes and procedures
- Drafting and preparing HR policies, contracts, letters, employee handbooks and associated documentation
- Completing high volume HR administration accurately and efficiently
- Maintaining accurate and up to date employee records
- Handling sensitive and confidential employee information with complete discretion
- Supporting clients with HR and employment law related queries
- Keeping knowledge of UK employment law and relevant legislation up to date
- Producing professional written correspondence, including letters, templates and emails
- Communicating professionally with clients via telephone and email
- Updating and maintaining HR systems and databases
- Ensuring all documentation is completed with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Providing general administrative support to the wider HR team as required

Skills and Experience Required
The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Significant previous experience within an HR Administrator, HR Assistant or HR support position
- CIPD Level 3 qualification or currently working towards a recognised CIPD qualification
- A good working knowledge of current UK employment law
- Experience drafting HR documentation, including policies, contracts, letters and employee handbooks
- Experience maintaining employee records and handling confidential information
- Strong knowledge of GDPR and the importance of confidentiality when dealing with employee data
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- A professional and confident telephone manner
- The ability to articulate themselves clearly and professionally when communicating with clients
- Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage a high volume workload
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office
- Previous experience using Breathe HR software would be advantageous, although experience with similar HR systems will also be considered
- A proactive approach to keeping knowledge of employment law and HR legislation current
- The ability to work independently whilst also contributing effectively as part of a team
Due to the office location, candidates must be able to drive and have access to suitable transport.

The Benefits
- £27,000 annual salary
- Monday to Friday working hours
- 9:00am to 5:00pm
- 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
- Your birthday off each year
- Pension
- Free onsite parking
- Opportunity to gain broad HR exposure across a diverse portfolio of clients
- Opportunity to develop your knowledge of employment law and outsourced HR
- Excellent opportunity for continued professional development and progression within HR

About the Role
This position would suit an experienced HR Administrator who enjoys variety and wants to build broader HR experience.
Rather than supporting one organisation, you will work across a portfolio of different clients, providing outsourced HR support and assisting with a wide range of HR processes and employment law matters.
The successful candidate will be professional, articulate and highly organised, with excellent written communication skills and a genuine interest in developing their HR career.
If you have previous HR administration experience and are looking for an opportunity where you can continue developing your HR and employment law knowledge, we would love to hear from you.
Apply today for immediate consideration.

Thank you for your interest in this vacancy, which is being advertised by SMT Recruitment Group, acting as an employment agency/business. Your application will be considered alongside other applicants, and we will contact you within three working days if you have been shortlisted.
SMT is a multi award winning specialist recruitment consultancy focused on the supply of temporary, contract and permanent placements across a select group of business sectors.

title: Network HR Assistant
description:
Do you enjoy being at the heart of HR operations, keeping everything running smoothly behind the scenes? Are you at your best when juggling multiple sites, priorities, and stakeholders? Looking for an HR role where consistency, accuracy, and strong relationships really make a difference?

GXO is currently recruiting a Network HR Assistant to support our B&Q retail logistics operation. This role plays a vital part in delivering consistent, high-quality HR support across a number of unionised operational sites during a period of continuing integration and change. You'll be a trusted presence across the region, supporting managers and colleagues with the day-to-day employee lifecycle while ensuring policies, processes, and data standards are applied consistently.

This role is being offered on a part-time, permanent basis. The hours of work are 37.5 per week, 5 days per week, predominantly Monday to Friday, office hours. Some flexibility will be required, this is logistics after al!

Pay, benefits and more:

You'll be paid a salary of up to £28,500 per annum. You'll also receive 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), as well as the option to buy additional days so you can enjoy a positive work-life balance. Your benefits package includes flexible dental insurance plans, a company sponsored pension scheme, a 24/7 online GP service, life assurance and a fully comprehensive employee assistance programme. You'll also have access to our MyBenefits platform offering a variety of high street discounts, a cycle to work scheme, cashback cards, a saving scheme and much more! Including our GXO University which provides you the opportunity to learn new skills and gain qualifications at a pace that you're comfortable with.

What you'll do on a typical day:
- Provide end-to-end HR assistance across multiple sites, including contracts, variations, starters, leavers, right-to-work checks, references, and probation tracking
- Maintain accurate HR systems and personnel files, ensuring GDPR compliance at all times
- Support employee relations activity by preparing documentation, tracking case timelines, and note-taking at meetings
- Coordinate recruitment and onboarding activities, including adverts, interviews, offers and pre-employment checks
- Produce regular HR reports including headcount, starters/leavers, absence and probation milestones
- Act as a first point of contact for HR admin queries, escalating appropriately where required

What you need to succeed at GXO:
- Proven experience in a high-volume HR assistant or coordinator role, with a good working knowledge of HR systems and employment documentation
- CIPD Level 3 is desirable, with support available for further development.
- Confidence supporting operational, unionised environments (or a strong willingness to learn)
- Strong attention to detail and pride in producing accurate, well-organised work
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple locations
- Clear, professional communication skills at all levels

We engineer faster, smarter, leaner supply chains.

GXO is a leading provider of cutting-edge supply chain solutions to the most successful companies in the world. We help our customers manage their goods most efficiently using our technology and services. Our greatest strength is our global team - energetic, innovative people of all experience levels and talents who make GXO a great place to work. GXO is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate, support and thrive on diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We believe that diversity and inclusion in our business is critical to our success as a global company, and we seek to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool.
